note: Three runs: 0.980 / 0.980 / 0.985. Lowest recorded, per-vertical from that run. The prompt did NOT change - the fingerprint is identical to the previous record - and the re-measurement was forced by SCOPE: Semantic added 24 calibration cases, 176 -> 200, and the gate requires the recorded count to equal the live set. That gate exists because a measurement over 120 of 168 cases once passed as family-wide for eight days. SEMANTIC SHIPS WITH NO JUDGE BODY, and that is a finding rather than an omission. Bitemporal and Temporal each needed one because each had a real collision with the shared preamble - 'the correction had not been recorded yet' reads as premature, 'nothing happened between them' reads as missed. Semantic has no such collision: measured at 0.958 in all three runs with nothing but the preamble and StandardBody, comfortably clear of the 0.80 per-vertical floor, and NO case fails in every run. THE DISCIPLINE THAT PRODUCED THAT ANSWER: 24 controls were authored BEFORE any body existed and a baseline was measured first. Two of my own labels failed that baseline. cal-sem-009 was simply wrong - I labelled a TRUNCATED company name correct, and preamble rule 3 already says missing detail gold treats as part of the answer lowers the outcome; the control was fighting an existing rule instead of testing a new one, and is now a paraphrase rather than a truncation. cal-sem-020 I relabelled abstained -> wrong, and that was overconfident too: pooled over eight runs the judge splits exactly 4-4 there. Had the body been written first, both labels would have been enforced by a template and Semantic would have shown a flawless 24/24 - the Bitemporal overfit again, one week later. WHAT REMAINS IS NOT SEMANTIC'S. Every flapping case in this record - cal-for-006, cal-for-012, cal-for-013, cal-wm-012, cal-sem-007, cal-sem-020 - sits on the same abstained/missed/wrong seam, now visible across FOUR verticals. The shared preamble lists 'I have no record of that' under ABSTAINED and 'you never told me about that' under MISSED, and they are near-synonyms. On this evidence that ambiguity is the largest remaining source of judge instability in the family, and it is parked for its own controlled change with its own controls and a before/after across all eight verticals.
